Issued at 357 AM EDT Mon Aug 24 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Broad ridge remains in place over the southwestern US...but northern 
axis is being shunted eastward into the Upper Midwest attm as an 
upper low tracks across southern Canada, deepening as it goes. 560dm 
500mb low encompasses the Lower Great Lakes, centered just east of 
Georgian Bay...with a 1003mb occluded surface low as a response. 
Cold air mass (+8C at 850mb overhead attm) associated with this 
feature resulting in a tight thermal gradient and attendant 100+kt 
upper jet wrapping from Lake Superior through the Mid-Atlantic, and 
up through New England and eastern Canada. Return flow through the 
Plains aiding in a plume of moisture stretching from central Canada 
ahead of aforementioned upstream trough, down into the Lower MS 
Valley and around to the Canadian coast, along/ahead of a surface 
boundary from disturbance in Saskatchewan...wrapping back around the 
upper low over eastern Canada. Warm/moist advection wrapping around 
the backside of the low into the Upper Great Lakes, with strong low-
level flow through the Soo into Lake Huron. Area of stratiform rain 
wrapping down across the eastern half of the CWA attm with a few NW 
flow lake effect/enhanced showers showing their face as of 5z near 
and west of I-75.

Ridge axis to slide overhead today...and will expect the influence 
of the upper low and filling surface low to further wane as we go 
through the day. Upstream upper low crests the longwave ridge axis 
Tuesday and begins to track southeastward into the Upper 
Midwest...bringing our next shot at rain/storms. This feature 
appears to slow a bit, crossing the Upper Great Lakes at some point 
Wednesday/Wednesday night. Upstream ridging strengthens over central 
Canada in its wake...with some energy attempting to enter western 
Canada...and an upper low developing over Hudson Bay that should try 
to scoop up our midweek system. This suggests we will remain in the 
presence of a baroclinic zone for late week...and with cool/cold, 
cyclonic flow influencing our weather again, would anticipate 
unsettled weather will prevail. Attm...quite a bit of uncertainty in 
the evolution of the forecast for the end of next week, depending on 
when Pacific energy attempts to eject through the flow, which should 
increase return flow through the central US and should keep the 
unsettled idea going into the end of August. Ridge axis over central 
Canada may get pinched quite tightly, but there are some signals it 
may try to hold on going into next weekend...and will certainly need 
to keep an eye on this for some kind of blocking pattern to develop 
to our north. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Lingering breezy conditions and rain showers today...Strongest winds 
will be this morning into early afternoon, with sustained winds 
remaining around 10-15kts, but the pressure gradient will be 
diminishing, and think there is a reasonable shot we could end up 
with light/variable winds after dark tonight as high pressure builds 
in. Plume of richer moisture (both in an absolute and relative 
sense) looks slow to depart, especially northeast Lower, and think 
this is where there will be a better shot at seeing more persistent 
rain/drizzle today...though not impossible things could stay a 
little more drizzly near Gaylord with northwest flow upsloping 
through the day, and there could be an uptick in coverage in the 
afternoon with a niblet of PV looking to swing through. However, 
there are not terribly strong signals for forcing attm, and have 
suspicions we may not end up with much more than scattered/broken 
stratocu. 

Rain/storms Tuesday night-Wednesday...We could start to see the 
first inklings of at least mid/high clouds by Tuesday afternoon 
ahead of the next system...though not impossible some rain showers 
may try to sneak in during this time. Better theta-e advection 
enters the scene Tuesday evening into Tuesday night as the system 
looks to take shape a little better upstream ahead of the digging 
trough, and this this is the more likely timeframe for rain and 
thunderstorms to move in...perhaps as some sort of upstream 
convective feature/dying convective feature that crosses the lake? 
Though this could bring a warm nose that could take most of the day 
to overcome...but it currently appears we have potential for several 
hundred joules of elevated instability to work with, which could 
become surface-based in the afternoon if we warm enough. With 
marginal (30ish kts, give or take) deep-layer shear in play, think 
we will need to keep an eye out for some storm organization as well. 

Absolute moisture increases again along/ahead of the associated cold 
front Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, perhaps up towards 
1.5in...and with signals for reasonable synoptic forcing to work 
with, and perhaps not overly fast storm motions...will need to 
monitor for heavy rain potential right on into Wednesday night.
